grade: C- (correct directional bias overridden by excessive caution; sizing/conviction mismatch)
observations: <parameter name="provisional_lessons">["When aggressive call and conservative call diverge sharply (stand_aside vs 0.55 short) and price is chopping near a wall (7448-7450 tagged almost exactly per the 15:00 aggressive read), the market often needs one more failed test before it breaks — the read was right, timing/patience was the gap, not direction.", "At 14:30 the aggressive short thesis was flat-out wrong (market ripped +53 to 7450 instead of breaking down) — this is a reminder that 'no support below' reasoning near a wall can fail badly if the wall itself gets broken upward first; walls can flip from resistance to launchpad.", "Once the top was actually tagged (7450) at 14:45/15:00, the subsequent moves were huge clean breakdowns (-60, -107, -79 pts) that were flagged correctly in direction and even in the specific target zones (7405-7395, 7395), but conservative stand_aside missed nearly the entire move — being 0.3 conviction stand_aside three cycles in a row while aggressive kept calling the same fade-short thesis and kept being validated is a pattern worth watching: repeated aggressive conviction that later proves right should probably start upgrading the conservative stance sooner.", "The 15:10 'short (0.4)' call finally aligned conservative with the actual move, but by then most of the 100+pt drop was already captured only by the aggressive line, not by the more cautious default — suggests conservative threshold may be miscalibrated to react only after confirmation that costs most of the move.", "One session is not enough to conclude 'always trust aggressive over conservative near identified walls' — this could easily be a case of a lucky sequential read on a trending gamma unwind day; need more days with mixed/choppy outcomes to see if aggressive calls get punished as often as they get rewarded."]

Overall regime: strong persistent uptrend all day, spot ~7668 (10:30) to session highs ~7758 (15:46) before a sharp late fade to 7736.5 close. Every dip was bought; no meaningful reversal materialized until the final 20 minutes.

Conservative model stood aside for ~95% of the day (0.55-0.85 confidence stand_aside), missing the entire ~90pt uptrend from 7668→7758. Only flipped to 'long'/'short' briefly at 11:25 (long, correctly, after price already up ~34pts) and again 14:43-14:44 (short, which was WRONG — price rallied from 7740 to 7755 after that short call, a real miss/loss setup).

Aggressive model was long almost continuously from 10:38/10:40 (@7675.63) through repeated hold/trail instructions, riding the move from 7675 to peak entries around 7750-7755 — this was the single best decision of the day, capturing the bulk of the ~80pt trend.

Aggressive round-tripped through several re-entries (7675.63 -> implied exits/re-adds at 7689.79 (11:08), 7703.91 (11:39), 7709.49 (11:56), 7718.03 (12:32), 7745.91 (14:53), 7750.91 (15:01), 7755.17 (15:20)) — each new entry chased a higher king_node/wall level as price kept breaking through. This trend-following re-entry cadence worked well on the way up.

Around 13:30-13:38 aggressive flipped to a SHORT scalp at 7734.69 targeting 7725, explicitly countertrend against the day's dominant uptrend. Price never came close to 7725 — it continued higher to 7745+ over the next 45m (max_down only -1.3, max_up +17). This countertrend short was a clear LOSER, and the model's own notes for later re-entries (14:40-14:49 short from 7740.37 targeting 7726) also failed to hit target; price only dipped modestly before resuming to make new highs (7755+) — another countertrend short that underperformed vs simply staying long/flat.
14:50 aggressive explicitly exited the short 'thesis invalidated' — good adaptive discipline, avoided compounding the countertrend loss.

Late day (15:09 onward): after price tagged 7755 king node and pushed to session high 7758 at 15:46, it reversed HARD, dropping from 7758 to 7736.5 by the 15:55-16:00 close (a ~21pt round-trip down). Any long entered in the 15:01-15:46 window (7750.91, 7755.17, 7756.5, 7758 chase) would have been sitting on open losses at the close (max_down readings of -16 to -21.5 in the final entries) — the last few 'long' aggressive calls (15:45, 15:46 chasing 7756.5/7758) were poorly timed, buying right at the top of the range into the eventual reversal.

The wall/king-node framework (7700, 7715/7725, 7740, 7755, 7770) correctly identified sequential resistance levels that price paused at before breaking through each time on the way up — useful map, though the model was consistently too conservative on trim targets (e.g., repeatedly capping targets at 7695/7698/7699 under the 7700 wall) versus letting the position run, which would have captured much more (spot eventually reached 7758, ~60pts beyond the first 7698 cap).

15:55 EOD-flatten mentality (conservative/aggressive both stand_aside heavy by 15:50-16:00) avoided being long into the final reversal — this effectively saved money since the 15:46-15:47 chase-long entries were the ones caught by the reversal; the model had NOT added new size in the last 10 minutes, which was protective.

grade: B (aggressive), C- (conservative) — good trend capture mid-morning, but consistent early exits left large money on the table, and afternoon chop chewed up both sides with repeated stop-outs
observations: Morning: two false long attempts (09:59, 10:01, both SPXW calls) into what the arc later confirms was a "down" trend forming — both stopped for -747/-561. The 09:59 decision-arc row itself showed max_up=0, max_down=-27.9 in the following 45m — the long thesis was fighting the tape from minute one.
10:27 arc correctly flagged "chop" then by 10:42 flipped to "down" with agg 0.72 — the short pivot was well-timed and is the best decision of the day.

From 10:30-11:18 aggressive ran a cluster of SPXW puts (7770P, 7775P x2, 7760P) all hitting target for +3354/+1996/+1788/+1190 — this is the day's engine. All four captured only 40-64% of the underlying's post-entry move before the shared 11:18 target/exit wave. Spot kept falling to 7724-7731 over the next 30-40min (per 11:12 and 11:26 arc rows showing low_next 7731.1 and 7724.9) — a huge amount of continuation was left unharvested because every position on the board hit the SAME target time (11:18) rather than a staggered/runner exit.

Conservative book mirrored this: 7755P and 7760P shorts captured only 21-48% of the underlying move, consistent with target being set too close to entry given the trend had real legs (spot dropped another ~30pts after these exits per 11:12/11:26 arc).

11:18->12:21 aggressive short (7755P) and conservative 11:19->12:20 short (7760P) show the flip side: once the easy trend leg was harvested, chasing the SAME direction into 11:54-12:08 chop/reversal (spot bounced 7724->7744, max_up 19.2 at 12:08) caused give-back — stop-outs, near breakeven.

Midday chop (12:22-13:47): long 7740C (-816), long 7730C (-259), three QQQ put scalps all stopped within minutes (-454/-147/-308) — arc conviction here was low (0.3-0.55) and "chop" labeled, yet trades were still taken. This is the classic theta-tax pattern: five straight small-to-medium losers in a directionless regime.

Late day: 15:26 arc flipped "up" (long taken, stopped +298 partial), then 15:39-15:50 short 7735P got hit for -1434 as spot fell hard into close (7723.1) — thesis flagged "invalidated" and exited manually just before the real drop that would have made it a winner; classic sold/covered wrong side just before the move validated in the other direction. Ironic: the short direction was right for the close but the position was already flattened on a stop/invalidation call before the actual friendly move showed up by 15:59.
Net day: big aggressive short cluster (+8328 gross) offset by chop/short-side/wrong-way trades; likely net positive but efficiency-dragged.
provisional_lessons: HOLD-TO-TARGET: Today undercuts blind "hold to target" as currently calibrated — targets on the 10:30-11:18 short cluster were clearly too tight relative to trend continuation (spot fell another 20-40pts after every target hit). Same target level triggering 4 separate positions simultaneously (11:18) is a strong tell that the target is a fixed distance dial, not adaptive to trend strength.

FORCED EXITS: No evidence today that stops "saved" money on the trend side — the trend shorts that stopped out later (11:18->12:21 aggressive, 11:19->12:20 conservative) did so on a *counter-trend bounce* (12:08 max_up 19.2), so those stops likely were correctly protective, not costly. But the 15:39 short "thesis invalidated" exit right before spot dropped hard into the close looks like a costly premature exit — worth flagging for pattern-check across days: are "thesis invalidated" exits systematically mistimed near turning points?

TREND-COMMITMENT: Strongly supported today. The two counter-trend long attempts at the open (09:59, 10:01) both failed immediately against a developing down day. The pivot to short at 10:30-11:18 once "down" trend was confirmed produced the day's entire profit. Trading WITH confirmed trend >> guessing reversals early.

THETA-TAX & CONVICTION: Standing metrics still show conviction is near-degenerate (81% of all 68 trades at exactly 0.55) — today's data added more 0.55-conviction trades on both winning and losing sides (e.g., 0.55 shorts that won big, 0.55 longs that lost immediately), reinforcing that the number carries little discriminating information yet. The one weak positive signal: today's higher-conviction trades (0.65-0.72 shorts in the 10:30-11:18 cluster) were the biggest winners, consistent with the standing bucket table showing 0.6-0.8 buckets outperforming 0.5-0.6. But sample size at high conviction remains tiny (still only 2 trades >0.7 historically) — not enough to call this validated.

EXIT EFFICIENCY / SOLD-TOO-EARLY: This is today's clearest, most costly pattern. Every winning short in the 10:30-11:18 cluster captured only 40-64% of the underlying's favorable move, and the two conservative winners captured only 21-48%. On what was clearly a real trend day (spot fell ~65pts from 10:42 to 11:26), running FOUR separate same-direction positions to the SAME nearby target instead of holding at least one runner toward the 11:26-12:08 lows (7724-7731) left a large amount of the move unharvested. This directly supports the "sold-too-early is the #1 trend-day tax" hypothesis — today is a strong single-day data point for it, though still just one day.

Additional hypothesis to track: taking trades in "chop"-labeled regimes at low conviction (0.3-0.55) produced a clean losing streak (5 straight stops midday) — supports tightening or skipping entries when arc explicitly says "chop," but need more days to confirm the chop-labeled subset is systematically -EV.
